ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 16616), as amended, Articles 5-2 and 5-3; Act on Regulation and Supervision of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 16618), as amended, Articles 3 and 6; Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 17207), as amended; Commercial Act (Act No. 17255), as amended, Articles 289-317; Supreme Court Registration Rules; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, as amended, Articles 16 and 28; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) AML/CFT guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Certificate of Existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the jurisdiction in which the foreign investor is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the certificate locally, obtain an apostille from the Apostille Convention competent authority, and submit the apostilled original to Korean counsel. Consular path for non-Apostille states: notarize the certificate locally, obtain any required foreign affairs verification, then legalize at the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that issuer jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence, No Litigation, and No Tax Debts where available)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry and/or revenue authority maintaining official corporate status records in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the certificate and apostille it through the designated central authority of the Apostille Convention state. Consular path for non-member states: notarize, have the certificate verified by the relevant foreign ministry, and legalize it at the Korean consular post. The two authentication paths must be used in the alternative and never combined or chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the Korean office formation agent and legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor, notarized in the jurisdiction of the investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the investor's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, the notarized board resolution must be apostilled by the competent authority; no consular act is added. If the jurisdiction is not a member, the notarized resolution must be legalized by the Korean embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive paths; the same instrument cannot undergo both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Articles of Association (Charter and Statutes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor through its board or the official company registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille state: authenticate the certified copy at the local notary, take the authenticated document to the designated apostille office for an apostille certificate, and deliver the apostilled copy to Korean counsel. Non-Apostille state: authenticate at the local registry, verify at the foreign ministry, and obtain consular legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate. Never chain both paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Bank Reference Letter from the beneficial owner's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank's head office through a duly authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a bank in an Apostille Convention state: the bank officer's signature is notarized, then the document is apostilled by the competent authority; no consular legalization is required. For a bank in a non-member state: notarize the signature and then legalize the bank letter at the Korean consulate in the bank's jurisdiction. These two paths are exclusive alternatives and must not be applied as consecutive steps.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every proposed director, shareholder, UBO, and authorized signatory must undergo screening against (i) the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit's guidance under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information; (ii) the US OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists; (iii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, including Democratic People's Republic of Korea targeted sanctions; (iv) the Korean government's independently designated financial sanctions measures maintained under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; and (v) domestic PEP databases covering the National Assembly, high-ranking public officials, judiciary, military commanders, and state-owned enterprise executives. Enhanced due diligence requires source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation for any individual holding 25% or more of shares, all beneficial owners, and persons with direct or indirect control. Any sanctions or PEP hit must be escalated immediately to the compliance partner for negative news review and, if unresolved, must cause rejection of the formation mandate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS), the official online portal for name existence and registry conflict checks
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name of a Chusik Hoesa must be expressed in Hangul characters. A foreign word or brand may be transliterated into Hangul following the statutory Korean-language transliteration guidelines; Latin or Roman alphabet script may be used only as a supplementary trade name, not as the sole registered name. The four-tier naming convention comprises: (1) distinctive identifier, (2) corporate form suffix indicating Chusik Hoesa, (3) business objective clause, and (4) registry-assigned distinguishing characters or serial number when needed. The registry rejects any name that is identical or misleadingly similar to an existing company name engaged in the same business within the same administrative jurisdiction.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must file a written objection with the head of the district court registration office within 14 days of the notice, restating the legal basis for distinctiveness under Korean Commercial Act Articles 22 and 23. The registry must issue a reasoned determination. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may apply for an immediate appeal to the competent High Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, attaching the previously proposed Hangul name and corrected trade-name alternatives, no later than 14 days after the refusal decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a voice streaming social application company classified as ISIC 6311 and using only Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not per se forbidden at the incorporation registry level, but it is highly likely to be rejected for National Tax Service business registration and corporate bank account opening. The Commercial Act requires the registered office to be the principal actual place of business; the National Tax Service and Korean banks insist on a physical lease, management substance, employees, and operational records. A commercial mail-forwarding address without any staff or lease will be treated as a paper company and will trigger enhanced verification, tax filing rejection, or refusal of a bank account.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspection by the Seoul Regional Tax Office or municipal registry authority: Low (5-10%) if the office has a registered written lease in the company name, company signage, stored corporate books, resident staff, payroll records, utility bills, and a visible business-registration certificate. Moderate-to-High (25-40%) if a virtual office, shared desk, serviced address, or mail-forwarding service is used. Required physical-inspection checklist: (1) lease contract registered by the landlord; (2) rent paid from a corporate bank account; (3) business registration certificate posted at the address; (4) payroll and insurance records for Korean employees; (5) board minutes executed at the registered office; (6) utility and internet charges in the company name.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Online company name clearance and registry index search through IROS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory official fee for the online name-search and availability function; access is free of charge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Korean translation of certificate of incorporation, articles of association, board resolution, good standing certificate, and bank reference letter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized sworn translation agency recognized for Korean registry submissions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of approximately USD 130 per standard translated page for a five-page documentary bundle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille or consular legalization of the mandatory documentary bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Apostille Convention competent authority, or Korean Embassy/Consulate as applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory and consular fee schedule; apostille fees are USD 0-20 per document plus courier; consular legalization fees are USD 50-70 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing and PEP/sanctions screening against OFAC, UN, KoFIU, and Korean domestic sanctions databases
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed international corporate compliance and sanctions screening provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat market benchmark of USD 300 per UBO for the identified three individual ultimate beneficial owners.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation Korean government court registration and registration license tax fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean District Court Registry Office and local municipal tax authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean Registration and License Tax Act based on 0.4% of stated capital plus the court registration fee, calculated assuming KRW 100,000,000 stated capital; final amount depends on registry computation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel professional fees for Stage 1 pre-incorporation due diligence, name clearance, UBO interviews, and drafting of the incorporation decision memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cross-border corporate law firm acting as Korean formation counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 400-450 per hour for senior associate time, fixed-fee agreement for Stage 1.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000 of 1962, as amended), Part III, Chapter II, Articles 288 through 316 (in particular Articles 289, 292, 293, 294, 295, 300, 302 and 317), read together with the Notary Public Act and the commercial registration rules of the Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry Division (Hoesa Deunggi-gwa) of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered head office in the Republic of Korea; online filing through the Internet Registration of Corporations (i-REG) portal run by the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of the Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa (Company Incorporation Registration Application) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, accompanied by the notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation and the paid-in capital certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under Korean law: no statutory floor on paid-in capital applies to a Chusik Hoesa. Shares must be fully subscribed and the subscription price must be fully paid before registration; a bank paid-in capital certificate is required. No blocked escrow account is required by the Commercial Act. Practical capital may be KRW 10,000,000 or more to qualify for venture-company certification, but this is a fiscal policy option, not a legal minimum.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [CORPORATE NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE INITIAL DIRECTORS.

WHEREAS, the undersigned individuals have been validly appointed as the initial directors of [CORPORATE NAME] (the "Company") by the incorporators' instrument of subscription and the certificate of incorporation; and WHEREAS, the Company has been registered with the Corporate Registry Division of the District Court in accordance with Articles 288 to 316 of the Commercial Act and is now lawfully authorized to commence its corporate affairs; NOW, THEREFORE, upon due notice and by unanimous written consent of all initial directors, the following resolutions are hereby adopted, effective upon registration:

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. The Board confirms the entire subscription and payment of the initial number of shares by the subscribing shareholders, records the amount of paid-in capital stated in the certified articles, and authorizes the representative director to execute the certificate of payment, the statutory registers, and all documents required for the perfection of the capital subscription.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board fixes and adopts the registered office of the Company as the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation and the certificate of incorporation. The representative director is directed to file all necessary notices and registrations with the district court, the National Tax Service and any other competent authority, and to take all necessary steps to maintain a physical place of administration for service of legal process.

3. BANKING AUTHORITY. The Board hereby opens and authorizes banking facilities with a licensed bank in the Republic of Korea and authorizes the representative director and the financial officer, jointly, to open deposit, settlement and corporate settlement accounts, sign KYC documents, execute bank mandates, and make initial payments of taxes and registration expenses.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board resolves to appoint the following mandatory officers: the representative director; the financial officer; and the corporate secretary, each with the powers and duties provided under the Company's Articles and the Commercial Act. The corporate secretary is authorized to sign all filings, to make all statutory filings, and to keep corporate seal custody, books, registers and minutes.

5. GENERAL MATTERS. The Board authorizes the officers, with the power to sub-delegate, to obtain all operating permits, tax registrations, telecommunications-application authorizations and digital-content compliance certificates, and to engage outside counsel, provided this resolution shall be construed broadly and no further act shall be required.

ADOPTED this [DAY] day of [MONTH], [YEAR] at [CITY], Republic of Korea.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Commission of Korea; Corporate Name Search through i-REG of the Supreme Court of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search through the Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration of Corporations search engine to ensure the proposed company name is not identical or deceptively similar to any existing Chusik Hoesa within the same business objective. Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation, containing the corporate objective covering interactive audio chatroom and voice streaming social application services, the number and par value of shares, total subscribed capital, address of the registered head office, method of public notice, and the term of directors. Submit the draft to a notary public for certification; all incorporators must sign personally or through a verified power of attorney. The notary will verify the certificate of capital payment and certify that the articles contravene no mandatory provision of the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Reserved corporate name confirmation or name search printout
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passport or corporate certificate of each incorporator
Power of attorney (if the incorporator is a legal entity or absent)
Proposed registered office address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search or notary queries the articles, amend the deficient clause by unanimous incorporator consent and re-notarize; if the proposed name is rejected by the registry search, submit a revised articles with an alternate name and pay a new research fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Subscription Price and Verification of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital subscription account at a licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea under the corporate name exactly as stated in the certified copy of the proposed corporate name. Each subscriber shall transfer his, her or its full allotted subscription price to the temporary account; the bank shall issue a certificate of balance or deposit certificate attesting the aggregate paid-in capital and the account holder. If any incorporator is a foreign person or entity, obtain a foreign exchange certificate of acquisition and a source-of-funds declaration for anti-money-laundering compliance. This paid-in capital certificate will be annexed to the notarized articles and submitted to the registry to evidence full payment under Article 292 of the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Temporary capital subscription account application form
Proof of payment or wire transfer receipt for each subscriber
Certificate of deposit or balance from the commercial bank
Passport / corporate identification and AML/KYC forms
Foreign exchange acquisition report if any consideration originates abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to certify because of a name or KYC discrepancy, cure the discrepancy with corrected corporate documents, re-issue the power of attorney, or close and reopen the temporary account in the final registered name before the incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through i-REG
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application with the Corporate Registry Division of the district court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office, either in person or through the Internet Registration of Corporations portal. Submit concurrently the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital payment certificate, written consents of the first directors and statutory auditor, and proof of payment of registration license tax and education surcharge. The registry will examine the application to confirm that the matters set out in Article 317 of the Commercial Act are recorded, that the paid-in capital is fully subscribed, and that the notarial formalities were completed. If the application is in order, the court will assign a corporate registration number and issue a certificate of registered matters.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa
Notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Bank paid-in capital certificate
Written consent / notice of appointment of first directors, auditor and representative director
Registration license tax and education surcharge payment receipts
Specimen signature / seal declaration of the representative director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementation order, file the omitted or corrected documents within the prescribed two-week cure period; if registration is refused, file an incidental appeal against the registration decision before the competent appellate court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Insurance and Digital-Compliance Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service; National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service; relevant telecommunications regulator if triggered
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days of incorporation, file the business registration application with the district tax office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered office, and obtain the corporate taxpayer registration certificate. Register the corporate seal at the same tax office, open the definitive corporate settlement bank account, and register for corporate income tax and value-added tax. If employees are hired, file mandatory registrations with the National Pension Service, the National Health Insurance Service, the Employment Insurance agency and the Workers' Compensation agency. For a purely digital voice-streaming social application, no industrial manufacturing or environmental license is triggered; nevertheless, if the service provides open communication to Korean users, assess whether value-added telecommunications business registration under the Telecommunications Business Act must be made, based on the final product architecture, and in all cases install privacy and personal-information protection controls required by the Personal Information Protection Act before commercial launch.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration (certificate of registered matters)
Business registration application form under the Value-Added Tax Act
Corporate seal and corporate seal registration certificate
Lease agreement or proof of registered office
Power of attorney of the representative director
Identification documents of officers and shareholders (for tax identification)
Personal Information Protection Act checklist for the digital service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service returns a query, correct and resubmit the defective form with the corporate registration certificate and lease agreement; if late registration penalties are assessed, pay the penalty and file a request for discretionary reduction based on justifiable cause, or amend the registration within the voluntary correction window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activity. The company is a pure digital interactive audio chatroom and voice streaming social application operator under ISIC 6311, and therefore does not require an industrial production license from any Korean municipal industrial agency.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, VOC emission source, hazardous waste generation, or air pollutant stack exists. The activity is excluded from the Korean Clean Air Conservation Act, Water Environment Conservation Act, and Waste Control Act permitting schedules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no dedicated industrial or warehousing premises require a Civil Defense fire-safety certificate, structural load inspection, or manufacturing workplace safety approval. Only ordinary office workplace fire-extinguisher and electrical installation safety obligations apply under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea; online portal Home Tax Service (Hometax) at hometax.go.kr; Korea Customs Service at customs.go.kr is competent for customs export clearance and export declaration matters; licensed Korean foreign exchange banks administer inward remittance reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information System under the Ministry of Economy and Finance
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity commencing Korean VAT-taxable activities must obtain a Korean business registration number, which is the unified taxpayer identification number and VAT registration number. For a foreign corporation with no Korean domestic place of business but supplying electronic services to Korean customers, the NTS provides a simplified registration pathway for foreign electronic service providers under the VAT Act. The procedure is: 1) confirm whether a Korean domestic place of business exists; if none, appoint a Korean tax representative in accordance with the Framework Act on National Taxes; 2) prepare the foreign entity constitutional documents, board resolution, apostilled or notarised corporate existence certificate, and power of attorney for the Korean representative; 3) file the business registration application with the competent NTS district tax office or the designated Hometax registration center for foreign electronic service providers; 4) submit proof of the Korean business address for a physical establishment, or for a purely F-type remote digital supplier, submit evidence of the electronic marketplace activity, the foreign entity legal details, and the tax representative appointment; 5) obtain the NTS-issued 10-digit business registration certificate; 6) for cross-border electronic services, apply for the simplified VAT registration classification and receive the assigned VAT ID; 7) maintain this ID for quarterly VAT returns and electronic tax invoice reporting. For a Korean Chusik Hoesa, the domestic incorporation process automatically generates the corporate registration file and the initial business registration application is made to the district tax office; the business registration number is used for both corporate tax and VAT compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; the Republic of Korea does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity classification election. A Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily a domestic corporation taxed at the entity level under the Korean Corporate Tax Act; pass-through status is unavailable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act; a single national VAT with no subnational sales-and-use tax overlay
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for domestic Korean businesses: any person carrying on a VAT-taxable business in Korea must register with the NTS before making taxable supplies. Foreign non-resident suppliers of electronic services, including voice-streaming and app-marketplace services consumed in Korea, also have mandatory Korean VAT registration with no KRW revenue threshold; the zero-threshold rule applies to overseas electronic service providers under the VAT Act and its Presidential Decree.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The NTS operates the Hometax electronic tax invoice system. Registered businesses must issue e-Tax Invoices for B2B supplies and transmit them to the NTS within the statutory filing deadlines, with automated cross-matching against the counterparty's VAT returns. There is no separate pre-supply anti-fraud digital stamping or customs clearance authorisation for ordinary VAT invoices; instead, the NTS performs real-time receipt and matching of e-Invoice data using Hometax and its API-based filing channels. Foreign electronic-service providers under simplified VAT registration must file returns and pay through Hometax, and must preserve transaction-level records showing the customer, service description, amount, foreign-currency settlement, IP-geolocation and consumption-location logic. For payments routed through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing, the Korean taxable entity must additionally retain app-store commission statements, remittance reports, and evidence of the Korean end-user vs foreign end-user split to support VAT treatment and export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies under Article 21 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act where goods are physically exported from Korea and where services are supplied to non-resident persons and actually consumed outside Korea. For the voice-streaming social app scope, the Korean supplier may claim 0 percent VAT on supplies to overseas end users only if it can prove foreign consumption through foreign user IP address or device jurisdiction, foreign app-store listing and billing location, non-Korean payment rails, and no Korean user access in respect of that transaction. Export services under invoice and contract must be in foreign currency and the proceeds must flow back into Korea through a licensed foreign exchange bank or through foreign app-store remittance channels. If the recipient or consumption is in Korea, zero rating is denied and standard 10 percent VAT applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration Certificate (export clearance certificate) for physical goods exports
Commercial invoice and export/service contract evidencing the foreign buyer and delivery term
Bill of Lading, seaway bill or airway bill for tangible merchandise; not required for pure digital voice-streaming services but must be retained for mixed goods transactions
Foreign exchange inward remittance confirmation or foreign exchange settlement certificate from a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank showing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
App-store settlement reports from Apple IAP or Google Play Billing showing gross receipts, commissions, territory of sale and net remittance to the Korean entity
Overseas end-user evidence including IP geolocation logs, mobile country code, billing address, payment metadata and usage session logs demonstrating foreign consumption
Hometax zero-rated sales schedule and supporting ledger reconciling each zero-rated supply to the foreign exchange evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS determines on audit that export zero-rating was claimed without valid documentation or that the service was consumed in Korea, the exported supply is reclassified as taxable at 10 percent and the VAT underpaid is retrospectively assessed with statutory penalty surcharges under the VAT Act and Framework Act on National Taxes. Intentional submission of forged export declarations, false remittance certificates or fabricated foreign-user evidence can trigger criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment or a criminal fine, and the tax authority may reopen prior tax periods within the statutory assessment window. Exporters also risk the suspension of export VAT refunds, the denial of future zero-rating claims, customs compliance sanctions from Korea Customs Service, and adverse foreign exchange reporting penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for non-repatriation or late repatriation of export proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange policy authority, the Korea Customs Service for trade settlement declarations, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) for AML reporting
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA), the Korean won is fully convertible for current account items, including software and digital content export proceeds, without prior central bank approval. The capital account, however, is liberalized on a 'negative list' basis: transactions are permitted unless specifically restricted, but must be channelled through a designated foreign exchange bank and reported indirectly via that bank. Inbound foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa requires a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; the inward remittance is then freely credited to a capital escrow account. Profit repatriation, whether dividends, capital gains or liquidation proceeds, is treated as a current account remittance for the foreign shareholder, subject only to documentary proof of distributable reserves, audited financial statements, withholding tax clearance with the National Tax Service, and a Foreign Exchange Transaction Reporting filing. There is no surrender requirement and no quantitative restriction on conversion, but all settlements must be evidenced with a Foreign Exchange Certificate issued by the receiving bank. A de facto practical hurdle is the conservative bank scrutiny and the physical documentation standard rather than any legal convertibility ceiling.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The statutory surrender requirement was officially abolished in 1999; Korean exporters may retain 100% of foreign currency export proceeds in a foreign currency account with a licensed foreign exchange bank. For service exports, including digital content and app-store receipts, the exporter must receive the proceeds through an authorized bank within a settlement period of one year from the date the service is rendered, and any extension beyond the period requires a statement of justifiable cause submitted to the designated foreign exchange bank. Upon settlement, the bank issues a foreign exchange receipt certificate used for zero-rated VAT refund and export credit support. While no fixed percentage of conversion to KRW is mandated, the customs and tax authorities require the company to demonstrate actual repatriation of export revenue; a mere contractual right without inward remittance is not recognised as taxable zero-rated export turnover.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (KRW) and Foreign Currency Operating Account (USD multi-currency)
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) with integrated USD FX current account
Basic KRW Settlement Account plus Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for offshore digital EMIs. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, any person performing foreign exchange business, money transmission, or payment services in Korea must register with the MOEF or operate as a licensed foreign exchange bank. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Revolut and other neobank-style platforms do not hold a Korean foreign exchange business licence and cannot provide a domestic clearing account, KRW IBAN equivalent, or local FX settlement for a Chusik Hoesa. A domestic entity's treasury must therefore be anchored at a licensed bank; an offshore EMI may only act as a supplementary payout aggregator if, and only if, it routes funds through a licensed Korean partner bank, and the bank's compliance committee will treat such aggregators as unapproved correspondent channels for a Medium-Risk Enhanced entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. Korean banking rules, aligned to the Financial Action Task Force recommendations and the Korean Financial Supervisory Service standards, require the statutory representative (CEO or registered director) to appear in person at the branch for the opening interview and identity verification. For a non-resident foreign director, the bank will accept only an original or consular-apostilled passport and, if available, a valid Alien Registration Card; a fully remote or consular proxy opening is not permitted for a foreign-owned Medium-Risk Enhanced corporate account. A local attorney-in-fact may complement the process, but only with a notarised and apostilled power of attorney, the corporate certificate of shares, and a board resolution, and even then a video call underwriting interview with the foreign director is additionally required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity in the cross-border shareholding chain of the Chusik Hoesa, where foreign shareholders hold indirect control and the corporate ledger is not immediately transparent to the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete UBO cluster: KoFIU-compliant beneficial ownership declaration forms for every natural person holding 10% or more of shares; certified passport copies of all such individuals; notarised corporate registry extracts and articles of incorporation for each intermediate holding vehicle, apostilled and translated into Korean; the Korean Registry of Commerce certified certificate of registered matters reflecting the full ownership chain; and a 12-month bank statement and source-of-wealth letter substantiating the funding for the initial share capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model exposure: voice-streaming, virtual gifting and companion social features may attract romance-scam, fraud or other third-party criminal proceeds, and the bank will question whether the app can identify the ultimate funder of each transaction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive AML/CTF policy and transaction monitoring manual for the Korean entity; product architecture evidence that all user top-ups are exclusively settled through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing with no anonymous prepaid cards or crypto on-ramps; a monthly reconciliation layout linking each app-store purchase receipt to a distinct user account; content moderation and user-verification logs; and a signed commitment letter to provide the bank with quarterly app-store payout statements and ongoing transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement mismatch: high-volume, low-value inbound app-store revenue versus limited local operating expenditure may indicate pass-through financing, trade-based money laundering or unregistered remittance operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A three-year cash-flow and treasury forecast showing salary, hosting, licensing and marketing costs; monthly Apple/Google payout statements with gross sales, commissions and net remittance details; a legal opinion confirming that the Korean entity is the true service provider and not a shell intermediary; and an executed undertaking to wire in real-time MT940 or camt.054 bank statements to the bank's digital oversight portal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP and adverse-media exposure of foreign directors and non-resident counterparties, which triggers enhanced due diligence and potential rejection at the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit screening stage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Police clearance certificate or its equivalent from the country of residence of every director and major shareholder; a signed PEP and sanctions self-declaration form; a negative-media and sanctions-screening run on each beneficial owner against UN, OFAC, EU and Korean FIU lists; and certification that all app-store settlement counterparties (Apple and Google) are licensed or recognised payment processors operating from compliant, non-sanctioned hubs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital for the Chusik Hoesa must be reported as foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, with the foreign investor filing the investment report through the designated bank. The capital is then remitted by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for the cover) with the statutory Korean foreign exchange purpose code for inward direct investment, e.g., establishment of a corporation or acquisition of shares, and wired into the Capital Escrow Account opened in the company's name at the Tier-1 bank. The receiving bank verifies the remitter against the FDI report, issues a Foreign Exchange Certificate, and the law firm completes the capital verification with the Korean Registration Court; the escrowed KRW funds become operational once the paid-in capital is registered. No proceeds may be disbursed until the capital registration certificate is filed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound cash payments for royalties, content licensing, cloud infrastructure and vendor services are executed through SWIFT MT103 with the applicable FETA service-transaction purpose code, supported by the underlying contract, invoice and tax invoice. For physical goods (not expected in this app-only model), commercial letters of credit under UCP600 and documentary collections (DP/DA) would be available through the bank's trade desk, but for a pure voice-streaming operation the bank will clear vendor payments through its corporate electronic banking portal via the local KRW clearing (HOFNET) for domestic vendors and via MT103 for cross-border SaaS and creative partners. All FX conversions from the app-store foreign currency receipts into KRW are executed as spot conversions with trade settlement records retained for transfer-pricing and VAT zero-rating audits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD FX forwards with a maximum tenor typically up to twelve months, available only against underlying projected app-store export receipts and dividend or royalty obligations, documented with the corresponding Apple and Google payout forecasts
FX swaps for temporary conversion of USD settlement receipts into KRW working capital with mandatory re-conversion for the same underlying export exposure

Cross-currency interest rate swaps and structured FX-principal swaps are permissible only for non-speculative hedging of long-term offshore debt or capital expenditure; the bank will require an annual hedge-effectiveness and underlying-exposure certificate

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are unavailable to onshore Korean residents for KRW and any offshore NDF referencing the won is strictly prohibited; the treasury blueprint must therefore remain with onshore deliverable hedging with no speculative overlay

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders with approval of annual financial statements, election or re-election of directors, and appointment or reappointment of statutory auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance record; resolutions changing registered particulars must be lodged with the Commercial Registration Section of the competent Korean District Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, the Annual General Meeting must be convened by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No government filing fee for the meeting itself; failure to register a director or auditor change within 2 weeks may trigger an administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 under Article 635 of the Korean Commercial Act and makes the change unopposable to bona fide third parties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration of changes in directors, representative directors, statutory auditors, registered office, and share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the Korean District Court with jurisdiction over the registered headquarters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks from the date of the corporate event, including annual re-election, resignation, removal, CEO change, capital change, or relocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Event-driven registration taxes and court fees apply; late registration is subject to administrative fines up to KRW 5,000,000, and unregistered changes may not be asserted against good-faith third parties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax return, tax base report, and settlement of corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year companies must file by March 31; a one-month extension to April 30 is available for companies subject to statutory external audit and filing through a licensed tax professional under applicable National Tax Service conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% of unpaid corporate tax for non-filing, 10% additional tax for underreporting, and daily late-payment interest at the National Tax Service statutory rate of approximately 0.022% per day; persistent non-compliance can lead to tax seizure and criminal referral

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax return and payment of the local surtax on national corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government, including Metropolitan/Provincial tax authorities, through the WeTax local tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate income tax deadline; March 31 for calendar-year companies, or April 30 if the extended external-audit deadline applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax additional charges of 20% for non-filing, 10% for underreporting, plus daily overdue interest under the Framework Act on Local Taxes; local tax collection may be enforced through seizure of assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax periodic returns covering digital content, voice-streaming platform revenue, and input VAT reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year period January 1 to June 30: file by July 25; second half-year period July 1 to December 31: file by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file carries 20% additional tax on VAT payable; understatement of tax base carries 10% additional tax; excess refund claims carry 10% additional tax; daily late-payment interest accrues at the National Tax Service statutory rate; separate penalties apply for failure to issue or revise electronic tax invoices

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit of financial statements and filing of the independent auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission, Financial Supervisory Service, and the electronic disclosure system DART for public-interest or threshold-triggered companies; the audit report must also be presented to shareholders at the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent auditor's report must be completed in time for the Annual General Meeting held by March 31; for DART filing companies, the audited annual report is due within 90 days after fiscal year-end, and the audit report must be received by the company and, where required, submitted or disclosed within 2 weeks after the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies may result in corrective orders, public disclosure of violations, administrative fines, restriction of the external auditor, and for listed or public-interest companies, listing agency and Financial Supervisory Service sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise change report for non-resident shareholding or cross-border capital movements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance through Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency or a designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the date of any change in registered foreign-invested enterprise information, including share transfer to or by a foreign investor, additional investment, capital reduction, change of representative, or relocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violations of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act may result in penalties up to KRW 10,000,000 or imprisonment up to 5 years in aggravated cases; the foreign investment may also lose statutory protection and tax/transaction privileges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance and annual internal verification of statutory books and registers, including the shareholders register, minutes books, and supporting corporate records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No governmental filing in ordinary cases; the records must be available at the registered office for shareholder inspection, court order, or audit inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation with records updated as events occur; annual document audit should be completed by the Annual General Meeting date and no later than March 31 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain statutory registers or to deliver inspection documents may expose directors to administrative fines and civil liability; under the Korean Commercial Act, fines of up to KRW 5,000,000 may be imposed for noncompliance with court-ordered inspection or delivery orders

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified public accountant audit is legally mandatory for a Chusik Hoesa if any one of the following criteria is met: (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion as of the immediately preceding fiscal year-end, which is approximately USD 9.0 million at an exchange rate of 1,333 KRW/USD; (ii) the company is listed on KOSPI, KOSDAQ, or KONEX, or is otherwise designated as a public-interest corporation; (iii) the company is a financial institution, securities firm, insurance company, or another entity expressly required by sectoral statutes to appoint an external auditor; or (iv) the company is designated by Presidential Decree as requiring an external audit for investor protection or public interest. Turnover and headcount alone do not create a statutory audit mandate under Korean law; the decisive quantitative balance-sheet trigger is the KRW 12 billion total-assets threshold, with transitional KRW 7 billion thresholds applying to certain earlier comparative fiscal periods under the Enforcement Decree.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Services Commission is mandatory for listed companies and public-interest corporations; non-public companies may apply K-GAAP, the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, or the Korean SME Accounting Standards where eligible. A company subject to statutory external audit must apply one accounting framework consistently and present comparative financial statements in accordance with that framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose an annual UBO declaration in the style of offshore registry jurisdictions. Instead, the applicable protocol is event-driven and continuous: (i) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign investor acquiring or transferring shares of the Chusik Hoesa, or changing registered foreign-invested enterprise particulars, must file a change report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance through KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days of the triggering event; (ii) the company must maintain its shareholders register accurately and update ownership transfers before transferring voting or dividend rights; (iii) if the company transacts with a financial institution or falls within AML-regulated activities, beneficial owners must be identified and verified, and material changes in beneficial ownership communicated to the counterparty or reporting institution; (iv) the Korean Commercial Act does not require an annual UBO confirmation filing to a corporate registry, but the register of members must be physically available for inspection at the registered office and must reflect all transfers as of each shareholders meeting date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages if security interests over company assets are issued or registered
Minute Book of Shareholders' General Meetings
Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings
Merchant Books and Supporting Accounting Documents

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (statutory top marginal rate; progressive brackets of 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Applicable incentives include: (i) 5-year corporate tax holiday (100% reduction) followed by 50% for the next 2 years for qualifying foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones and Incheon Free Economic Zone; (ii) R&D tax credit under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, with up to 30-40% of qualifying R&D expenditures creditable for SMEs and 2-3% for large enterprises; (iii) tax breaks for venture enterprises under the Venture Business Promotion Act (income tax/corporate tax 50% reduction for 5 years in certain regions); and (iv) special deductions for job creation and facility investment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Beobinsae Gwaeseopyojun mit Saeae Singojang) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing system (hometax.go.kr); official form number processed as Form 40-1.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, plus semi-annual interim prepayments (mid-year and year-end) for corporations with taxable income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final Corporation Tax Return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., for a calendar-year company, by March 31 of the following year). An extension of up to one month is available for qualified companies upon application. Interim prepayments are due within two months after each six-month fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification, resident registration, and tax representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean corporate registration number (business registration number), legal entity type (Chusik Hoesa), representative director name, and head office address. If the corporation is foreign-invested, attach the foreign investment report certificate and state the percentage of non-resident ownership. For companies wholly owned by foreign shareholders, the filing must designate a domestic tax representative (if the company is not managed and controlled from Korea) to ensure service of process and compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income and revenue, including sales of digital content, membership fees, and voice-streaming service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue from Korean-source activities, including app store sales via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing denominated in KRW or foreign currency. Where revenue is received through overseas payment gateways, convert to KRW using the official exchange rate and attribute the income to the Korean operating entity. Do not exclude Korean-source digital revenue merely because the billing intermediary is a foreign-controlled entity; such receipts may still be deemed taxable in Korea. If fungible services are performed offshore, apply transfer pricing rules and disclose related-party service agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating deductions, cost of goods sold, employee compensation, depreciation, and other deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dedicate particular scrutiny to payments made to related foreign companies, including royalties, management fees, commission fees, and interest on intercompany loans. Deductions for payments lacking a valid business purpose or failing the arm's-length standard are disallowed. Under the Korean thin capitalization rule, interest paid to a controlling foreign shareholder in excess of a 150% debt-to-equity ratio (200% for finance companies) is not deductible and is recharacterized as a dividend subject to withholding. All intercompany transactions exceeding the statutory threshold require Local File / Master File documentation to be retained and produced upon NTS request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for exempt income, tax-exempt reserves, R&D credits, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim statutory tax credits for qualified R&D (software development costs can qualify if documented). For foreign-invested enterprises qualifying for free-zone incentives, attach a copy of the investment approval and compute the exempt amount. Non-resident shareholders may also claim relief from double taxation through the foreign tax credit mechanism. Any tax credit for domestic production or employment must be substantiated; unsupported claims will be denied with penalty surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income: gross income minus statutory deductions, adjustments, and loss carryforwards; determination of domestic and foreign source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile book income with taxable income by adding non-deductible items (e.g., excess entertainment expenses, fines, taxes) and deducting exempt/non-taxable items. Confirm that the five-year carryforward period (as provided in the filing parameters) is applied to net operating losses from prior years. Provide a comprehensive transfer pricing adjustment schedule and any allocation of income to a non-resident permanent establishment if a branch election exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculation and payment summary: applying progressive rates, subtracting prepayments/credits/withholdings, and computing the net tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: After applying the progressive corporate tax brackets, subtract interim prepayments and any foreign tax credit. If the company declares dividends or makes an interest-equivalent payment to a non-resident shareholder, withhold and report WHT as required. For outbound dividends, the withholding rate is 20% national tax plus 2% local resident surtax unless a treaty reduction is approved. Ensure the beneficial owner tax residency certificate and Form for application of withholding tax reduction are attached to the return in order to invoke the DTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: If the return is not timely filed, a negligence additional tax is imposed at 20% of the unpaid tax if filed within one month after the due date; otherwise 20% plus a daily delay surcharge of 0.022% on the amount unpaid until the date of payment. Where the filed return understates taxable income, an additional tax of 10% of the understated tax (20% where the understatement is intentional) is imposed. A fraudulent return or willful non-filing constitutes tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to five years or a fine of up to twice the evaded tax; if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, the imprisonment term increases to up to ten years. In order to avoid such penalties, the filing must be accurate and supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing and BEPS documentation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national corporate tax withholding, plus 2% local resident surtax (10% surtax on the national tax), aggregating 22% on cash and stock dividends paid by a Korean Chusik Hoesa to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced dividend WHT rate under an applicable DTA, the payee must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, dated in the current calendar year; (2) submit a written Application for Reduction or Exemption of Withholding Tax on Foreign Investment (Form No. 25-2) to the NTS district office via HomeTax before payment; (3) provide a Beneficial Ownership Statement in which the recipient declares he/she/it is the true beneficial owner of the income, has not received instructions from any third party, and will not pass the economic benefit onward; (4) disclose the ownership percentage and holding period to demonstrate that the shareholding meets any minimum holding period under the treaty; and (5) file such documentation with the domestic payer so that the payer may withhold at the reduced treaty rate. If the withholding was already made at 22%, the non-resident may file a claim for refund within five years by submitting the same documents to the NTS together with an amended return, supported by the withholding tax certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory WHT of 20% plus 2% local surtax (aggregate 22%) on Korean-source royalty income paid to non-residents including for the use of software, IP, or rights in internet/social platforms. Interest: statutory WHT of 20% plus 2% local surtax (aggregate 22%) on Korean-source interest income, including non-guaranteed bonds, loans, and intercompany deposits. Applicable DTAs generally reduce these rates; under the OECD Model convention, interest commonly to 10% and royalties to 15% or 10%, but each treaty must be individually verified based on the residence country and entitlement to benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, taxpayers must prepare and retain a Local File where the aggregate amount of cross-border related-party transactions exceeds KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 8 million) in a fiscal year. A Master File is additionally required when the multinational enterprise group has consolidated revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more and the Korean entity's related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion. A CbC report is required if the group's consolidated revenue reaches KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime modeled on the UAE or BVI. However, the substance-over-form principle and the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) under the Framework Act on National Taxes, together with beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits clauses in Korea's double tax treaties, require companies to demonstrate genuine economic activity. For entities seeking incentives in Free Economic Zones, a CIGA (Core Income-Generating Activities) analysis is applied: the taxpayer must show that key decision-making and core profit-generating functions (e.g., development, marketing, and user support) are located in Korea. Where a Chusik Hoesa acts as a conduit for royalties or dividends without local substance, Korean tax authorities may disregard its separate existence, deny treaty benefits, reclassify income, and impose understatement penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing revenues from Korean users of the voice streaming app through a wholly owned Hong Kong / Singapore subsidiary without legitimate commercial substance, while the Korean entity's financial statements understate gross receipts, with the intent to avoid Korean corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (Article 3-1), intentional evasion of corporate tax by fraud or other wrongful act is punishable by imprisonment for not more than 5 years or a fine not exceeding two times the evaded tax. Where the amount evaded is at least KRW 500 million, the maximum imprisonment is raised to 10 years. In addition, under the Framework Act on National Taxes, an understatement surcharge of 10%-20% of the underreported tax is imposed, and daily late payment surcharges accrue at 0.022% until the deficiency is paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed or participated in the revenue diversion may be personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax under the principle of piercing the corporate veil when the corporation is a mere alter ego. They may also be blacklisted (subject to departure bans) by the NTS for tax arrears over KRW 100 million. Civilly, the company can recover damages for breach of fiduciary duty, and criminally the directors may be sentenced to imprisonment; the court may order restitution of diverted funds. Repeated offenders face aggravated sentencing in parallel tax fraud prosecutions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Non-Compliance / Improper Dividend Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring and paying a dividend to a foreign parent company while failing to withhold and remit the statutory 22% Korean WHT, or applying a treaty-reduced rate without obtaining the required Tax Residency Certificate or beneficial ownership declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 98 and 98-5 of the Corporate Income Tax Law and Article 2 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, a withholding agent who deliberately fails to withhold tax is liable for the uncollected amount plus a late payment surcharge. In addition, a separate surcharge of 20% of the unreported withholding is imposed. Criminal penalties apply for willful non-withholding under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act, punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine of up to twice the unpaid withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director responsible for authorizing the dividend distribution without withholding becomes jointly and severally liable with the corporation for the unpaid WHT, penalties, and interest. The NTS may issue a personal tax collection notice, attach personal assets, and impose a departure ban. If the court finds intentional disregard, criminal sentence of imprisonment can be imposed upon the director as an accomplice or principal of the offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Malpractice / Shell Company Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing an intercompany license agreement under which the Korean entity pays excessive royalties to a zero-tax related company registered in a tax haven, without economic justification and without preparing transfer pricing documentation; the arrangement is designed to shift taxable profits out of Korea and relies on a lack of substance in the payee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the tax authority may adjust the taxable income upward and disallow the excessive royalty deduction. An additional tax equal to up to 30% of the understated tax is imposed for failure to submit TP documentation or for transactions not at arm's length. For recurring noncompliance, an additional gross negligence penalty may apply. If the sham transaction forms part of a scheme to defraud taxes, criminal charges can be brought under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the agreements may be held personally liable for the tax deficiency under the alter ego doctrine, particularly where the intermediary has no real Board, office, or employees. Civilly, each director is exposed to a derivative action for the loss caused by the tax adjustment. Directors may be prohibited from leaving Korea, and if convicted of document fraud or tax evasion, face up to 5 years' imprisonment and fines. The NTS may also request cancellation of the company's legal entity registration in cases of repeated shell-company abuse.
